findings.title: Working-hours check computes `end` from the slot start and compares UTC time to organizer-local minutes
findings.body: `end` is `slotStartTime.hour()*60 + slotStartTime.minute()`, identical to `start` (line 141). It should include `eventLength`, so a slot starting inside working hours but running past `endTime` is not rejected here. Also, `slotStartTime` is UTC, while `workingHour.startTime/endTime` are minutes in the schedule's timezone, and `organizerTimeZone` is not applied. So slots can be wrongly dropped or kept for any non-UTC organizer. The `find` callback also returns true only for the 'outside' case and is hard to read. This runs in the new `workingHours` path, which is active for the first two call sites, because `...schedule` spreads `workingHours`. Fix by converting the slot to the organizer timezone and testing `start < startTime || start + eventLength > endTime`.

findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with `===` – branch is dead
findings.body: `dayjs(a) === dayjs(b)` compares object identity and is always false. The intended 'override with zero length (day off)' case therefore never returns true here. A day-off override (start == end) is only rejected if the later `isAfter` or `isBefore/isSame` checks happen to fire. Use `.isSame(...)` or compare `valueOf()`.

findings.title: Date-override offset sign and DST handling look inconsistent with slots.ts
findings.body: The offset is computed as `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1`. `dayjs.tz(date, tz)` reinterprets the date's wall-clock value in `tz`, so the offset is taken at a shifted instant and may be wrong across DST. The result is then added to `date.start`, and the date is compared with `slotStartTime.format('YYYY MM DD')` in UTC. `packages/lib/slots.ts:212-214` uses a different method (`dayjs(start).tz(tz).utcOffset()` with an invitee/organizer difference). Two different conversions for the same override make mismatches likely near DST or day boundaries. Please use one shared helper. The test only covers one timezone pair, with no DST case.

findings.title: `override.timeZone` may be undefined and `start.toString()` is a lossy parse
findings.body: `TimeRange.timeZone` is optional. If it is missing, `.tz(undefined)` falls back to the local or default zone, and the offset difference becomes wrong. `dayjs(override.start.toString())` re-parses a locale string with no millisecond precision. Use `override.start` directly. The offset is also computed twice per override in `startTime`/`endTime`, because `.add(offset).hour()` and `.minute()` are each recomputed; compute it once.

findings.title: New test covers only one timezone pair, and its comment is unclear
findings.body: The test asserts the same UTC slots for a +6:00 invitee. It does not test the `checkIfIsAvailable` changes (busy time with an override, working hours outside the override, or a day-off override). The comment 'it should return the same as this is the utc time' does not explain why the expected values are unchanged. Add cases that would fail on the working-hours and `===` bugs noted above.

summary: The new date-override and working-hours checks in `checkIfIsAvailable` have real bugs. The working-hours `end` equals the slot start. A dayjs `===` comparison is always false. The timezone offset logic differs from the one in `packages/lib/slots.ts`, and the tests cover only one case.
